note: Files fetched into the corpus that are deliberately NOT captured. A capture is committed and a corpus is not improved by being larger, so anything no parser here will ever read is kept out by name rather than by somebody remembering. Their provenance stays in the tool folder's sources.json and the file stays in originals/ on this machine, so nothing is lost and the decision is reversible by deleting a line.
why_the_folders: The race and tuning loggers below are the largest group and share one reason: they are time series, not readings. This application models live data as a reading with a value, a minimum and a maximum - what a scan tool prints during a session - and shows it that way on the session screen. A datalog of ten thousand rows of RPM against time is a different artifact for a different job; collapsing it to a min and a max throws away the only thing it is for, and keeping the series is something neither the schema nor the screen can hold. NG-4 says scan data is imported per session rather than streamed, and this is where that line falls.

skip.bimmerlink/originals/2025-07-29-21-50-54: A graph, not a report. It renders eight thousand lines of rotated chart axis labels ('sixa', 'yramirp') and holds no codes, no VIN and no vehicle - and at 2.3 MB it was the largest capture in the corpus. The BimmerLink CSV beside it is the data that PDF is a picture of.
